title: Employer Benefit Charging: The Notice of Claim and the Employer's Separation Response
content:
When a claim is filed, Employer Benefit Charging gives each base-period employer the chance to answer it. This chapter sets out the notice, who may answer it, and when an answer counts as timely.

## The notice of claim

The notice of claim is mailed to each base-period employer's address of record, or to its authorized agent, within the mailing business days after the claim is filed (2 business days in every charge class). It asks for the separation reason, the last day worked and the base-period wages.

## Who may respond

Only the employer or a third-party administrator holding its power of attorney may respond. The agent never answers the notice for the employer. A response received moves the position from noticed to responded.

## The response window

A response is timely only when it is received no later than the response window after the notice of claim mailing date. The window is counted in calendar days starting the day after the notice of claim mailing date, a response received on the last day is timely, and the window is never extended. The response window is 10 calendar days in every charge class.

- **The clock starts from** the notice of claim mailing date recorded on the employer's position for that claim; it is the Department's record of the mailing date that counts, not a date the caller gives.
- **Day one** is the day after the mailing date; the last day of the window is the tenth calendar day after the mailing date.
- **Comparison:** the response date must not be later than the last day. Receipt on the last day itself is timely.

| Hypothetical notice of claim mailing date | Response received | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 3 March | 13 March (the last day) | Timely |
| 3 March | 14 March (the day after the last day) | Not timely |
| 28 April | 8 May (the last day) | Timely |
| 28 April | 9 May | Not timely |

A request to extend the window does not change these results, because the window is never extended.

## Late responses

A late response is treated as timely only when the employer shows good cause.

The former clause "otherwise payments issued before the late response stay charged even if relief is later granted" is **no longer in force**. It is not applied as a rule of its own. For the relief credit of a protest decision and for the relief credit of a determination on a separation response, the class term that payments issued before a late response stay charged is applied only through the share by which a response received after the due date without good cause reduces that relief credit, and no payment is kept charged on that account beyond it.

## No response

A position with no response by the end of the window becomes chargeable without relief, and the missing response counts toward the pattern of failure.

## Basis Q&A

*If a response reaches the Department on the last day of the window, is it late?* No. A response received on the last day is timely.

*Can a contact-center agent complete the response for the employer during a call?* No. Only the employer or a third-party administrator holding its power of attorney may respond.
